stem: Of the 27 breast cancer samples in this study, how many were sequenced on both platforms?
choices: 25, with the remaining 2 run on nanopore only
27, with every sample run on both platforms
20, with the remaining 7 run on nanopore only
25, with the remaining 2 run on Ion Torrent only
answer: 25, with the remaining 2 run on nanopore only
label: Results · cohort

stem: For the 25 samples run on both platforms, how did nanopore compare with Ion Torrent on small variants?
choices: Every SNV and small indel found by Ion Torrent was also found by nanopore
Nanopore missed several small indels that Ion Torrent detected
Nanopore missed several exonic SNVs that Ion Torrent detected
The two platforms disagreed on roughly a fifth of small variants
answer: Every SNV and small indel found by Ion Torrent was also found by nanopore
label: Results · platform concordance

stem: In which gene were the three truncating variants detected by both platforms across this cohort located?
choices: BRCA2
BRCA1
PALB2
CHEK2
answer: BRCA1
label: Results · variants detected

stem: How many patients tested negative for clinically relevant variants on both sequencing platforms?
label: Results · negative cases

stem: What structural variant did nanopore detect in four patients that the Ion Torrent panel missed?
choices: A 312-bp intronic AluYa5 insertion in BRCA2
A 312-bp intronic AluYa5 insertion in BRCA1
A large exonic deletion spanning BRCA2 exons 3 to 5
A tandem duplication of BRCA1 exon 13
answer: A 312-bp intronic AluYa5 insertion in BRCA2
label: Results · structural variant

stem: How was the BRCA2 c.4504C>G variant found in the nanopore-only patients classified?
choices: As a variant of uncertain significance
As likely pathogenic on in silico evidence
As pathogenic on splicing evidence
As benign on population frequency
answer: As a variant of uncertain significance
label: Results · nanopore-only cases

stem: How was the deep intronic BRCA1 c.5333-898A>G variant confirmed after nanopore detection?
choices: By bidirectional Sanger sequencing
By RNA sequencing of patient transcripts
By a repeat Ion Torrent run
By droplet digital PCR
answer: By bidirectional Sanger sequencing
label: Results · deep intronic variant

stem: Why would the Ion Torrent panel used here have missed the deep intronic BRCA1 variant?
choices: Its design targets exons and nearby splice sites, not deep introns
Its read length is too short to span the surrounding repetitive sequence
Its variant caller filters out single-nucleotide changes in introns
Its coverage of BRCA1 drops below threshold in the larger introns
answer: Its design targets exons and nearby splice sites, not deep introns
label: Results · panel coverage

stem: What was the population-database status of the deep intronic BRCA1 variant?
choices: Absent from gnomAD version 4
Rare in gnomAD version 4
Common in gnomAD version 4
Conflicting reports in ClinVar
answer: Absent from gnomAD version 4
label: Results · deep intronic variant

stem: What did SpliceAI and Pangolin both predict for the deep intronic BRCA1 variant?
choices: A novel cryptic donor splice site and activation of a pseudoexon
Loss of the native acceptor site of the downstream coding exon
Skipping of the adjacent coding exon in the mature transcript
Retention of the surrounding intron in the mature transcript
answer: A novel cryptic donor splice site and activation of a pseudoexon
label: Results · splicing prediction

stem: What delta gain score did SpliceAI assign the novel splice site, against the usual pathogenic cutoff?
choices: 0.84, against a cutoff of 0.2
0.84, against a cutoff of 0.5
0.62, against a cutoff of 0.2
0.21, against a cutoff of 0.2
answer: 0.84, against a cutoff of 0.2
label: Results · splicing prediction

stem: What did the two splicing tools predict near the primary gain event?
choices: A secondary gain event, scored 0.66 by SpliceAI and 0.62 by Pangolin
A secondary loss event, scored 0.66 by SpliceAI and 0.62 by Pangolin
A secondary gain event, scored 0.84 by SpliceAI and 0.81 by Pangolin
No further event above the reporting threshold
answer: A secondary gain event, scored 0.66 by SpliceAI and 0.62 by Pangolin
label: Results · splicing prediction

stem: What further evidence did Human Splicing Finder contribute for the deep intronic BRCA1 variant?
choices: New cryptic donor and acceptor sites, branch point and motif changes
A measured reduction in BRCA1 transcript abundance in patient blood
A predicted frameshift in the resulting BRCA1 protein sequence
A loss of the polyadenylation signal downstream of the variant site
answer: New cryptic donor and acceptor sites, branch point and motif changes
label: Results · splicing prediction

stem: What did splicing prediction show for the BRCA2 AluYa5 insertion, in contrast to the deep intronic BRCA1 variant?
choices: Delta scores below 0.2, so no splicing alteration was predicted
Delta scores above 0.8, so strong splicing disruption was predicted
Delta scores near 0.5, so the prediction was left indeterminate
A predicted pseudoexon matching the BRCA1 variant
answer: Delta scores below 0.2, so no splicing alteration was predicted
label: Results · splicing prediction

stem: How were BRCA1 and BRCA2 covered for nanopore sequencing?
choices: Six overlapping long-range PCR products for BRCA1 and four for BRCA2
Four overlapping long-range PCR products for BRCA1 and six for BRCA2
A single long-range PCR product spanning each gene
Hybridization capture probes tiled across both genes
answer: Six overlapping long-range PCR products for BRCA1 and four for BRCA2
label: Methods · long-range PCR

stem: How was the barcoded library from all samples sequenced on nanopore?
choices: On one R10.4.1 flow cell for 24 hours on a MinION Mk1C
On one R9.4.1 flow cell for 24 hours on a MinION Mk1C
On one R10.4.1 flow cell for 72 hours on a PromethION
On a separate R10.4.1 flow cell per patient sample
answer: On one R10.4.1 flow cell for 24 hours on a MinION Mk1C
label: Methods · sequencing run

stem: What was the Ion Torrent comparator in this study?
choices: A custom AmpliSeq panel covering 28 hereditary breast cancer genes
A custom AmpliSeq panel covering BRCA1 and BRCA2 alone
A commercial pan-cancer panel covering 135 driver genes
A whole-exome capture kit with breast cancer reporting
answer: A custom AmpliSeq panel covering 28 hereditary breast cancer genes
label: Methods · comparator panel

stem: How did the authors describe the up-front device cost of nanopore against the Ion Torrent platform?
choices: Roughly 10 to 20 times lower
Roughly 2 to 3 times lower
Roughly 50 to 100 times lower
Broadly comparable between the two
answer: Roughly 10 to 20 times lower
label: Discussion · cost

stem: Where did the authors expect the incremental benefit of long-read sequencing to shrink?
choices: On large multigene panels, where short-read stays more cost-efficient
On single-gene tests, where short-read coverage is already complete
In settings that lack local bioinformatics expertise and support
On samples with degraded or low-yield genomic DNA
answer: On large multigene panels, where short-read stays more cost-efficient
label: Discussion · scalability

stem: What testing model did the authors propose for combining the two technologies?
choices: Short-read for broad panels, with targeted long-read as a reflex test
Long-read as the primary method, with short-read for confirmation
Long-read replacing short-read across hereditary cancer testing
Both platforms run in parallel on every referred patient sample
answer: Short-read for broad panels, with targeted long-read as a reflex test
label: Discussion · proposed workflow

stem: Why could the splicing impact of the detected variants not be assessed directly?
choices: Patient RNA samples were unavailable, so no RNA sequencing was performed
The variants fell outside the regions covered by the RNA assay
Transcript levels were too low for reliable quantification
Ethics approval did not extend to transcript analysis
answer: Patient RNA samples were unavailable, so no RNA sequencing was performed
label: Limitations · functional validation
